problem: Sim-to-real gap in point-goal navigation: Bono et al. (CVPR 2024) injected real-world dynamics and sensor noise into simulated agents, but reproducing and validating this remains difficult, and simulated noise models are only approximations of a real robot.
motivation: Sim-to-real transfer for navigation policies is costly and hard to replicate. Running a physical robot inside a virtual world via XR could keep real dynamics while retaining experimental control. Only the abstract is available, so details are limited.
key_idea: Replicate Bono et al.'s dynamics-and-noise-injected point-goal navigation, then extend it with an XR-in-the-loop paradigm in which a physical AMR operates within virtual warehouse environments.
insight: The abstract reports no analysis or ablations; the claimed value is that XR-in-the-loop evaluation preserves real robot dynamics with virtual-scene control, which should improve replicability and give a more direct sim-to-real pathway. The paper says the method is only 'expected' to do this, so this is not yet demonstrated in the abstract.
method: Replication: rebuild the virtual point-goal navigation setup of Bono et al. (CVPR 2024) with the same evaluation metrics.

XR-in-the-loop extension: a physical autonomous mobile robot (AMR) is driven within virtual warehouse environments rendered through XR infrastructure, preserving real-world dynamics and sensor behaviour while keeping controlled virtual scenes.

setting.backbone: not specified in abstract (navigation policies from Bono et al.)
setting.simulator: virtual warehouse environments via XR (engine not specified); replicated virtual point-goal setup

results: The abstract reports no quantitative results; it states that the method is expected to enhance replicability and provide a more direct sim-to-real pathway.
limitations: Abstract only; no reported experiments or numbers, and benefits are stated as expectations.
Scope limited to point-goal navigation in virtual warehouse scenes with a single physical AMR.
builds_on: Bono et al. CVPR 2024 (sim-to-real via injected real-world dynamics and sensor noise)
